strings.name: Xu Bing
strings.role: Artist · Experiments in writing and visual systems
strings.summary: Born in Chongqing and raised in Beijing, Xu studied printmaking at the Central Academy of Fine Arts. Installations such as Book from the Sky combine printing, invented characters and reading experience. He later developed Square Word Calligraphy and pictogram narratives to examine how language structures cognition. He moved to the United States in 1990 and later returned to art education in Beijing. A MacArthur fellow and Fukuoka Prize recipient, he works across printmaking, installation, moving images and public projects.

strings.timeline.t1.title: Public lecture at HKU

strings.timeline.t2.text: Appointed vice-president of the Central Academy of Fine Arts, re-engaging with Chinese art education.

strings.timeline.t5.title: Square Word Calligraphy
strings.timeline.t5.text: Organized English letters into square forms resembling Chinese characters, exploring cross-cultural reading.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Moves to United States
strings.timeline.t6.text: Went to the United States at the invitation of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, expanding international work and exhibitions.
